citation: DFARS 252.204-7012(c)(1)(ii) and (c)(2); definition of 'rapidly report' in 252.204-7012(a)
trigger: Discovery of a cyber incident that affects a covered contractor information system or the covered defense information in it (both runbooks: enclave session theft; ransomware on Plant 2 MES and DNC, which hold CUI)
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery. Report what is known; add updates as the review continues
notify: DoD at https://dibnet.dod.mil, using a DoD-approved medium assurance certificate (252.204-7012(c)(3))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - subcontractor with DFARS 252.204-7012 in all current subcontracts
clock_starts: Discovery of the cyber incident (time recorded by the incident commander)
owner: Director of Trade Compliance and Contracts (Security Manager backup)

obligation: Review for compromise of covered defense information
trigger: Same trigger as the DoD report
deadline: Starts at discovery; results feed the report and its updates
notify: Internal (results go to DoD in the report)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - identify compromised computers, servers, specific data, and user accounts, including other systems that may have been accessed

obligation: Incident report number to the higher-tier contractor
trigger: After the DIBNet report is submitted and DoD assigns an incident report number
deadline: As soon as practicable
notify: Prime A, Prime B, and/or Prime C (whichever subcontract the affected CUI belongs to)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - flowed down in all current subcontracts
owner: Director of Trade Compliance and Contracts

trigger: Malicious software discovered and isolated in connection with a reported incident
deadline: As instructed by DC3 or the Contracting Officer. Do not send malware to the Contracting Officer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if malware is found (expected in the ransomware runbook; an adversary-in-the-middle kit may leave none)

trigger: Discovery of a cyber incident
deadline: Keep for at least 90 days from submission of the report, so DoD can request the media or decline interest
notify: Internal custody (Security Manager); forensic firm; cloud provider
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - images of all known affected systems, including MES and DNC servers, and relevant monitoring and packet capture data
clock_starts: Submission of the DIBNet report (90-day minimum)

obligation: DoD access for forensic analysis and damage assessment
trigger: DoD request for more information or equipment; Contracting Officer request for damage assessment information
deadline: On request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Director of Trade Compliance and Contracts is the DoD liaison; General Counsel reviews
owner: Director of Trade Compliance and Contracts

trigger: Incident involving CUI in the government-community cloud
deadline: The provider must comply with paragraphs (c) to (g); coordinate so reports and preserved data are consistent
notify: Government-community cloud provider (security contact from the CRM)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the company ensures the provider meets these duties

citation: DFARS 252.204-7012(m)(2)(ii) as flowed down to suppliers
trigger: A supplier that holds company CUI reports a cyber incident to DoD
deadline: The supplier gives its DoD incident report number to the company as soon as practicable
notify: Company receives it; the company informs the affected prime (contract practice, not a clause duty)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - for the 13 suppliers with current flowdown; the 9 legacy suppliers have no such duty until re-papered (P03 G-119)

trigger: Empowered Official believes an ITAR violation may have occurred (for example, technical data released to a foreign person)
deadline: Voluntary. Initial notice immediately after the violation is discovered; full disclosure within 60 calendar days of the notice unless an extension is granted (127.12(c)(1))
applies_at_this_tier: Decision by the Director of Trade Compliance and Contracts (Empowered Official) with export counsel. Theft by an outside attacker may not be a company violation; document the reasoning either way
owner: Director of Trade Compliance and Contracts

trigger: Company believes it may have violated the EAR (Customer D and Customer E parts carry EAR-controlled technology)
deadline: Voluntary; a deliberate decision not to disclose a significant apparent violation is an aggravating factor (764.5(a))
applies_at_this_tier: Decision by the Director of Trade Compliance and Contracts with export counsel
owner: Director of Trade Compliance and Contracts

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (employee records on the Plant 2 corporate segment or in SYS-11)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (one 15-day extension for good cause, provided in writing to the Department within 30 days)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if personal information is involved. Possible in the ransomware runbook (Plant 2 HR files); not expected in the exfiltration runbook
owner: General Counsel with the HR Director

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (the 15-day extension does not apply to this notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if 500 or more Florida residents' personal information is involved

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Only if more than 1,000 individuals are notified (the company has 850 employees, so only if former employees or applicants are included)

obligation: Third-party agent notice to the company
trigger: A third-party agent (for example, the payroll and HR SaaS provider) has a breach of the company's employee personal information
deadline: The agent must notify the company within 10 days of determining the breach
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - inbound duty on the agent; the company then decides individual notice

trigger: Personal information of residents of other states (for example, remote workers or former employees who moved)
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents and regulators per each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Only if personal information of non-Florida residents is involved

citation: Customer D and Customer E purchase agreements; services agreements (contracts)
trigger: Customer technical data or services customer files affected, or services disrupted
deadline: Per contract terms (services agreements: notice within 72 hours of confirming a security incident affecting customer data)
applies_at_this_tier: Contractual, not legal. Director of Trade Compliance and Contracts checks each agreement
owner: Director of Trade Compliance and Contracts

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy: call the carrier hotline before engaging vendors
notify: Carrier breach hotline ($15 million limit, $500,000 retention)
applies_at_this_tier: Contractual, not legal

obligation: Board and private equity sponsor update
trigger: Any incident declared severity 1
deadline: Within 24 hours of declaration
notify: Audit committee chair; sponsor's operating partner
applies_at_this_tier: Internal governance, not legal

trigger: Suspected theft of controlled technical information by a foreign or criminal actor; ransomware
deadline: As soon as practical
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Recommended; coordinate with the DIBNet report

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering any payment to an extortionist
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if extortion occurs. POL-03 4.11 requires a CEO decision after counsel, insurer, and OFAC check

trigger: Cyber incident on a classified information system
deadline: Immediately
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company has no facility clearance or classified systems

citation: FAR 52.204-25(d); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Discovery of covered telecommunications equipment or services during contract performance
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; mitigation details within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - not triggered by these incident types; applies only if such equipment is found (Plant 2 camera check, P01 R-039)
owner: Director of Trade Compliance and Contracts

trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at a public company
deadline: 4 business days after determining materiality
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is privately held

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports (PROPOSED)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours; 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; not a current obligation
